Dedicated to innovation and clinical excellence

At Massachusetts General Hospital, a founding member of Mass General Brigham, we are committed to providing the highest quality and safest care possible for every patient—near and far.

Home to the largest hospital-based research enterprise in the U.S., we foster a culture of collaboration and education, pushing the boundaries of medical research and maintaining an unwavering commitment to the diverse communities we serve.

Our expert clinicians are leaders in their medical fields and handle the most complex cases. Today, patients from around New England—and across the globe—trust us for their medical care. U.S. News & World Report ranks Mass General among the top 10 nationwide in psychiatry; ophthalmology*; cancer; rheumatology; diabetes/endocrinology; cardiology/heart surgery; and obstetrics/gynecology.

* In partnership with Mass Eye and Ear.

Onsite appointments

To request an appointment or learn more about our services, please complete the online form. Please rest assured that when you complete the online form, our team will personally contact you as promptly as possible. We aim to respond in fewer than 24-48 hours during the work week.

Many of our International services staff are multilingual. Should you choose to call us via the number below, we will do our best to communicate with callers in their native language. However, it may take a few minutes to get an appropriate linguist on the phone who can better assist you. For this reason, you may find it preferable to complete the form or email us with your initial questions in your native language. That will allow us to call you with a staff member who speaks your language.

Refer a patient

If you are an overseas physician and you would like to refer an international patient to Mass General Brigham or speak with us about potential care options for your patient, we would be happy to assist you.

Please contact us through this form, or you may email or call us. Our dedicated international referring physician team will promptly reply. We look forward to partnering with you in the care of your patients.

Massachusetts General Hospital and Brigham and Women’s Hospital patients

For all our international patients who know us as Massachusetts General Hospital or Brigham and Women’s Hospital, please rest assured we are all one team now. We have combined our international center teams into one coordinated effort across Mass General Brigham’s hospitals. If you’re an existing patient at one of our hospitals, you can submit your inquiries here and you’ll be promptly served by the same dedicated staff you’ve worked with previously.

Mass General Brigham Hospitals Named Among Nation’s Best by U.S. News & World Report

style
palette-deep-blue
showJumplinks
false

Mass General Brigham clinical services and hospitals were named among the best in the nation by U.S. News & World Report. Six hospitals within the system earned top national rankings, while the system’s institutes and clinical departments were also recognized for world-class specialty care. The rankings are a validation of Mass General Brigham’s sustained focus on high-quality care and patient outcomes.

The system’s founding members – Massachusetts General Hospital (MGH) and Brigham and Women’s Hospital (BWH) – were each named to the “Best Hospitals” Honor Roll, representing the top 20 hospitals in the nation. The system’s three Institutes in Cancer, Heart and Vascular, and Neuroscience also earned high marks.

Mass General Brigham’s three specialty academic hospitals – McLean, Mass Eye and Ear, and Spaulding Rehabilitation – also earned top rankings in their respective specialties. This year, Brigham and Women’s Faulkner Hospital (BWFH) also earned a national ranking (in Diabetes and Endocrinology), demonstrating the strength of the system’s Community Division.

“Mass General Brigham’s world-class clinicians and care teams provide the very best care for every patient who needs us, and this year’s rankings demonstrate our continued excellence in clinical care,” said Anne Klibanski, MD, President and CEO, Mass General Brigham. “Our relentless focus on high-quality outcomes continues to be our north star, especially as our integrated institutes and clinical departments shape the next generation of research-infused care.”

Top-ranked specialties and hospitals

  • Psychiatry: MGH ranked #1; McLean ranked #2; BWH ranked #14
  • OB-GYN: BWH ranked #2; MGH ranked #9
  • Rehabilitation: Spaulding ranked #2
  • Cancer: BWH and DFCI ranked #3; MGH ranked #5
  • Diabetes and Endocrinology: BWH ranked #3; MGH ranked #6; BWFH ranked #48
  • Ophthalmology: Mass Eye and Ear/MGH ranked #4
  • Rheumatology: BWH ranked #5, MGH ranked #6
  • Heart and Vascular: MGH ranked #6; BWH ranked #12
  • Neuroscience: BWH ranked #8, MGH ranked #14
  • Urology: BWH ranked #9; MGH ranked #17
  • Orthopedics: BWH ranked #10; MGH ranked #24

Mass General Brigham’s first-ever unified quality strategy, For Every Patient, is guiding the system’s approach to improving patient outcomes, which is anchored in high reliability and driven by a relentless focus on data and outcomes.

As  U.S. News & World Report  evolves its approach to focus more on these same outcomes, Mass General Brigham continues to perform at a high level. For the first time, this year’s rankings in Cardiology, Heart, and Vascular Surgery do not consider physician reputation, instead focusing primarily on 41 outcome measures. Amidst these methodology changes, Mass General Brigham’s net improvement in this category validates the system’s quality approach within its Heart and Vascular Institute.

Community division performance

Several Mass General Brigham community hospitals have also earned honors as high performers in several medical specialties and treatments:

Newton-Wellesley Hospital ranked #6 in the Boston Metro Area and #7 in Massachusetts (both tied with Salem Hospital). Newton-Wellesley was also recognized as High Performing in 14 procedures and conditions: back surgery (spinal fusion); COPD; colon cancer surgery; diabetes; heart arrhythmia; heart failure; hip fracture; hip replacement; kidney failure; knee replacement; leukemia, lymphoma & myeloma; lung cancer surgery; pneumonia; and prostate cancer surgery.

Salem Hospital ranked #6 in the Boston Metro Area and #7 in Massachusetts (both tied with Newton-Wellesley Hospital). Salem was also recognized as High Performing in Diabetes and Endocrinology; Geriatrics; and Pulmonology & Lung Surgery, as well as 11 procedures and conditions: COPD, colon cancer surgery, diabetes, heart arrhythmia; heart attack; heart failure; hip replacement; kidney failure; lung cancer surgery; pacemaker implantation; and pneumonia.

Brigham and Women’s Faulkner Hospital ranked #8 in the Boston Metro Area, #9 in Massachusetts and was nationally ranked in Diabetes and Endocrinology. BWFH was recognized as High Performing in Orthopedics and in eight procedures and conditions: COPD, diabetes, heart arrhythmia, heart failure, hip replacement, kidney failure, knee replacement, and pneumonia.

Cooley Dickinson Hospital was rated as High Performing in 3 procedures and conditions: hip replacement; knee replacement; and pneumonia.

About Mass General Brigham

Mass General Brigham is an integrated academic health care system, uniting great minds to solve the hardest problems in medicine for our communities and the world. Mass General Brigham connects a full continuum of care across a system of academic medical centers, community and specialty hospitals, a health insurance plan, physician networks, community health centers, home care, and long-term care services. Mass General Brigham is a nonprofit organization committed to patient care, research, teaching, and service to the community. In addition, Mass General Brigham is one of the nation’s leading biomedical research organizations with several Harvard Medical School teaching hospitals. For more information, please visit massgeneralbrigham.org.

What is Mass General Brigham Patient Gateway?

Mass General Brigham Patient Gateway is a secure electronic portal that helps you better manage your own health or the health of a family member. Patient Gateway allows you to do these things and more:

  • Communicate with your health care team
  • Schedule appointments
  • Participate in virtual visits
  • Review your medications and renew prescriptions
  • View lab or test results
  • Read visit notes and after-visit summaries
  • Request referrals
  • Pay your bill
  • Read health and wellness information

Parents, guardians, and adult children also can take advantage of these features to coordinate care for children, dependents, or parents.

  • Enroll in Patient Gateway

Patient Gateway is available in:

  • English
  • Arabic
  • Traditional Chinese
  • Haitian Creole
  • Portuguese
  • Russian
  • Spanish

How to use Patient Gateway

Patient Gateway is best used to make simple requests or review your health information. Here are some examples of appropriate and inappropriate use of Patient Gateway:

Do use Patient Gateway to:

  • Request non-urgent prescription refills.
  • Request scheduling of non-urgent appointments.
  • Send photos or information for the care team to review before an appointment.
  • View bills and make payments.
  • Securely message your care team for non-urgent medical concerns.
  • View health information, such as your medication list, test results, and screening tests you might be due for.

Do NOT use Patient Gateway to:

  • Make any urgent requests or ask urgent questions. Please contact the office with any urgent needs.
  • Send social or personal conversations, photos, and videos that are not related to health care.
  • Discuss complex medical issues or new severe medical symptoms. These are often best addressed in a visit with your provider or care team.
  • Ask questions about family members from your own Patient Gateway account.
  • Make complaints about other providers or care experiences. If you have concerns about your experience, please contact the patient relations office for the clinic or hospital.

These additional features are available:

  • Mobile app: Patients can easily access Patient Gateway using our mobile app. It is available for both Androidand iOS.
  • eCheck-in: Patients of practices using eCheck-in can verify and update insurance information, fill out questionnaires, and pay co-pays online before their appointment.
  • Virtual Visits: You may be able to sign onto a virtual visit from a link in Patient Gateway. Virtual visits can take place from home or another private location.
  • Information about your hospital stay: If you are admitted to one of our hospitals as an inpatient, you can see important information about your hospital stay. This information includes your inpatient medication list, who is on your care team and their progress notes, and education materials.

FAQs

How can I enroll in Mass General Brigham Patient Gateway?

Download instructions below on how to access Patient Gateway with an activation code or how to self-enroll without one.

Once you enroll, you can receive pre-visit questionnaires, appointment reminders, and use eCheck-in. You also can choose how you’d like to be notified about new Patient Gateway messages, including email or text messages.

Enroll with activation link

Enroll without activation link

Patient registration: 866-211-6588

I am a caregiver (spouse, parent, etc.) of a patient. How can I get access to their account?

A Patient Gateway patient care representative (PCR) account can be set up for patients. A Patient Gateway PCR is not the same thing as a health care proxy. A spouse, parent, adult child, or other designee may become a Patient Gateway PCR if they have been authorized by the patient. Please note that Patient Gateway access for teens and their PCR is limitedto meet state regulations for confidential teen care.

How can I get technical support?
Our team can help you address any questions or concerns. Read our FAQs or contact Patient Gateway Technical Support at 800-745-9683.

Patient and Family Advisory Councils

Mass General Brigham’s Patient and Family Advisory Councils (PFACs) bring together patients, family members, and hospital staff to improve the care experience. By sharing your insights, you can help shape hospital policies, programs, and services to enhance patient-centered care.

About PFAC

A Patient and Family Advisory Council (PFAC) is a group of patients, family members, and hospital staff dedicated to improving the care experience of patients and family members. PFAC members provide valuable insights, feedback, and ideas to help shape hospital initiatives, policies, and patient-centered care improvements.

What do PFACs do?

PFAC members help to improve the patient experience by:

  • Providing feedback based on their personal experiences as patients or family members.
  • Collaborating with hospital staff and clinicians on committees.
  • Lending patient expertise in discussion groups, educational sessions, and other strategic initiatives.
  • Reviewing and helping to develop educational materials for patients and families.
  • Assisting in hospital planning efforts to improve patient care and services.

What is a patient and family advisor?

A patient and family advisor is a patient, care partner, or family member who participates in a PFAC to provide insights based on their care experiences. Advisors help improve the quality and safety of hospital care by providing their unique perspectives on services, programs, and initiatives.

Who can be a patient and family advisor?

You may be eligible to become an advisor if you or a family member received care at a Mass General Brigham hospital in the past three years. No special qualifications are required — just a willingness to to collaborate, provide feedback, and contribute to meaningful discussions. Our goal is for our PFAC membership to reflect the diverse communities we serve.

Which PFAC should I join?

Every Mass General Brigham hospital has at least one general PFAC, which are open to all patients and family members who have received care at that hospital in the past three years. Some larger hospitals also have specialty PFACs, which focus on specific topic areas.

The following hospitals have General PFACs:

  • Brigham and Women’s Hospital
  • Brigham and Women’s Faulkner Hospital
  • Cooley Dickinson Hospital
  • Massachusetts General Hospital
  • Mass Eye and Ear
  • Martha’s Vineyard Hospital
  • McLean Hospital
  • Nantucket Cottage Hospital
  • Newton-Wellesley Hospital
  • Salem Hospital
  • Spaulding Rehabilitation (Including Boston, Cambridge, and Cape Cod)
  • Wentworth-Douglass Hospital

Brigham and Women’s Hospital and Massachusetts General Hospital also offer specialty PFACs* focused on specific care areas, such as:

  • Emergency Department (ED)
  • Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU)

*If you are interested in joining a specialty PFAC, contact us at pfac@mgb.org for more information.

How can I join a PFAC?

If you are interested in becoming a patient and family advisor, please fill out an application form here. Once we receive your application, we’ll reach out with the next steps.

Please note: You may only join one PFAC at a time, even if you are eligible for more than one. If you aren’t sure which PFAC is the best fit for you, email us.
